newsitem.title: ITALY: Fire hits Turin Cathedral, home of famous shroud.
newsitem.headline: Fire hits Turin Cathedral, home of famous shroud.

text.p: A huge fire engulfed the cathedral in the heart of this northern Italian city early on Saturday morning and threatened to spread to the adjoining royal palace, police said.

Italian news agency Ansa said the fire was believed to have started in a chapel which houses the famous Turin shroud -- a piece of cloth imprinted with the image of a man's body that many take to be the figure of Christ. Local officials said the shroud appeared to be safe.
Witnesses said flames were shooting out of one section of the roof of the 15th century cathedral, lighting up the night sky, as a large crowd gathered in the nearby central city square to watch.

Cathedral guards reported the fire shortly before midnight and Ansa said the fire brigade was struggling to contain the blaze. "This is an overwhelming tragedy," Turin mayor Castellani was quoted as saying.

"The fire brigade say they have gone into the...chapel and assure me the (Turin) shroud is safe," he added. Officials said later they believed that the cloth had been removed from the building and taken to safety.
It is the second time in a year that an historic Italian building has been damaged in a fire. Last year Venice's Fenice opera house was gutted by a blaze.
